Compilation succeeded. The deprecation note is just from `new Double(Double.NaN)` (deprecated boxed constructor), which is harmless.

Created `tests/com/google/gson/stream/JsonWriterAgentTest.java`, a self-contained JUnit 3.8 test class (extends `junit.framework.TestCase`) covering:

- Defaults (`isLenient`, `isHtmlSafe`, `getSerializeNulls`), and `Closeable`/`Flushable`/`AutoCloseable` contract
- Fluent return values (`beginArray`/`endArray`/`beginObject`/`endObject`/`name`/`value`/`nullValue`/`jsonValue` all return `this`)
- Compact vs. indented output (`setIndent`)
- Null handling: `nullValue()`, `value((String) null)`, `jsonValue(null)`, and `setSerializeNulls(false)` omitting object members (first/middle position) while leaving array elements unaffected
- Malformed-JSON `IllegalStateException` cases: unmatched `endArray`/`endObject`, mismatched begin/end, writing a second top-level value without lenient mode, `name()` outside an object, `value()` before a `name()`, repeated `name()` calls, and a dangling `name()` before `endObject()`
- Strict vs. lenient top-level values, and strict vs. lenient `NaN`/`Infinity` handling (`IllegalArgumentException` when strict)
- `name(null)` → `NullPointerException`
- Numeric/boolean encodings (`long`, `double`, `Boolean`, `BigInteger`), using tolerant double parsing rather than assuming an exact format
- `flush()` making buffered data visible without closing
- `close()` flushing and closing the underlying `Writer`, and throwing `IOException` on an incomplete document
- `setHtmlSafe` escaping `<`, `>`, `&`, `=` vs. default raw output
- I/O errors from the underlying `Writer` propagating as `IOException`
